title: Zelle limits: How much you can send per day
summary: What is the Zelle limit? Daily and monthly send limits vary by bank. See typical limits, whether you can raise them, and the alternatives. Read on.
body_markdown:
Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, and PayPal are leading peer-to-peer payment platforms that let you send and receive money using a phone number, email, or username. But unlike most other P2P services that have digital wallets, Zelle integrates with your bank app for bank-to-bank transfers.


One other clear distinction between Zelle and other platforms is the transfer limit. Zelle send limits are set by your bank, not by Zelle, so they vary widely. Many large banks allow a few thousand dollars per day and a higher monthly cap, while some smaller banks set lower limits. There is no receiving limit, and you usually can't request higher limits.


If you tried to send a larger payment through Zelle and hit an unexpected limit, the explanation lies with your bank, not Zelle. This guide explains how Zelle limits work, what typical ranges look like across major banks, and your options for sending larger amounts or transferring money internationally.


## What is the Zelle limit?


Zelle does not have one standard sending limit for everyone.[Zelle limits](https://www.zelle.com/faq/there-limit-how-much-money-i-can-send-or-receive) are set individually by each participating bank or credit union. Your Zelle limit depends entirely on the bank your Zelle is connected to. So two people using Zelle can have significantly different limits just because they use different banks.


Your bank sets the Zelle limit, which is capped at a specific daily or monthly amount based on its risk management policies, your account history, and sometimes your account tier.


There is also generally no receiving limit. Most banks allow you to receive money through Zelle without a specific cap, although very large payments may be reviewed for fraud or compliance reasons.


## Daily and monthly limits


Zelle limits typically apply on both a daily and rolling monthly (often described as 30-day) basis, and the specific figures vary meaningfully between institutions.


The typical daily limits across major US banks generally range from $500 to $10,000. However, some banks may set higher or lower rates. Some accounts, particularly newer accounts or those without extensive transaction history, may start with lower limits that can increase over time as the bank builds confidence in how the user transacts.


Some banks tie their Zelle limit to a fixed number of transactions. For example, Bank of America allows $500 over 10 transactions for new Zelle users. Business accounts often have higher Zelle limits than personal accounts.


Daily limits usually reset at midnight, though the exact time may vary by bank. Some banks also use a rolling 30-day limit instead of a calendar-month limit. This means your available limit depends on your total sent in the previous 30 days, not the calendar month.


Always verify your current limits in your banking app or by contacting your bank, as each bank sets and can change these limits at any time.


## Zelle limits by bank


The table below gives a general idea of the limits you may see at some major US banks for personal accounts. Business accounts usually have higher limits. These figures can vary by the account tier and are subject to change. Always confirm your current limit in your bank’s app or by contacting your bank’s support.

Verify with your specific bank before relying on these figures. Zelle limits change over time and can also vary within the same bank based on your account type, tenure, and transaction history. The most reliable way to confirm your current limit is directly within your bank's Zelle interface, in your banking app, or by contacting customer service.


## Can you increase your Zelle limit?


You may be able to increase your Zelle limit, depending on your bank’s specifications.


Your bank may increase your limit automatically after you use your account regularly and build a transaction history. Some banks also allow customers to request a higher limit through customer service or their banking app.


However, some account types have fixed limits that cannot be increased. Moving to a different account tier may increase your limit, but it depends on the bank.


You cannot ask Zelle to increase your limit because Zelle doesn't set individual sending limits. Any increase has to come from your bank or credit union.


## Sending larger amounts of money abroad


If you need to send more than your Zelle limit, you may need to wait for your limit to reset or split the payment across multiple days. This can be uncomfortable, especially when you need to complete the payment immediately. You might need to find an alternative payment option for a large domestic transfer.


Zelle doesn’t support international transfers. Zelle only works between eligible US bank accounts, so you cannot use it to send money to an international bank account. If you need to send money internationally, you'll need an alternative.


For larger domestic transfers within the US, you can use a same-day ACH or FedNow transfer through your bank. Your bank's ACH and FedNow limits are often higher than Zelle limits. You can also initiate a wire transfer for very large or time-critical amounts if you think the transfer fee is worth it.


For international transfers, you need a cross-border payment service to send money outside the US or to a non-US bank account. Traditional international wire transfers can be expensive because the sending bank, intermediary banks, and receiving bank may each charge fees. The receiving bank may also apply a markup when converting the money into the recipient’s currency. These transfers can also take up to five business days to arrive.

## Frequently asked questions about Zelle limits


### **What is the Zelle daily limit?**


There is no single Zelle daily limit that applies universally; each participating bank sets its own limit, generally ranging from $500 to $10,000 depending on the institution, account type, and account history. Check your current limit directly within your bank's Zelle interface, since it varies significantly by bank.


### **Does Zelle have a receiving limit?**


Most banks do not impose a specific limit on how much you can receive via Zelle, unlike sending, which is capped daily and monthly. However, unusually large incoming amounts may occasionally trigger a review for compliance or fraud prevention purposes, even without a formal receiving cap.


### **Can I increase my limit?**


Sometimes. Some banks automatically raise limits over time as you build a longer, consistent transaction history on the account. Others let you request an increase directly, though approval depends on the bank's policies and isn't guaranteed. Some entry-level account types have hard limits that cannot be increased regardless of request.


### **Why do limits differ by bank?**


Zelle does not set user-level sending limits; each participating bank sets its own limits based on its risk management policies, fraud-prevention approach, and account-tier structure. This is why the same person can experience very different limits simply by having accounts at different banks.


### **Can I use Zelle internationally?**


No. Zelle is a US domestic payment service that only works between enrolled US bank accounts. It cannot be used to send money to international bank accounts or to recipients outside the United States, regardless of the amount. For international transfers, you need a dedicated cross-border payment service.


### **How do I send more than the limit?**


Options include waiting for your daily limit to reset (typically at midnight) and splitting the payment across multiple days, using a same-day ACH transfer through your bank if the amount fits within your bank's ACH limits, or using a wire transfer for very large or time-critical domestic amounts. For international transfers, Zelle isn't an option regardless of the amount; you'll need a dedicated international transfer service like Grey instead.
